Choose an office chair that adjusts to your body and desk

Seat depth and arm height matter alongside capacity

Measure your desk clearance and compare seat-height and seat-depth ranges. A wide, high-capacity seat may be a poor fit if its front edge presses behind your knees or the arms stop you reaching the desk. Check whether the arms adjust, flip up or remain fixed. A maximum-weight claim is not an independent comfort test.

Plan for assembly and the return journey

Check the chair's assembled dimensions, base width and caster suitability for your floor. Lumbar support can be fixed, adjustable or simply shaped padding; inspect the actual mechanism. Look up return delivery and disassembly requirements before buying a bulky chair online. A footrest and deep recline are extras, not proof of good working posture or suitability for a full day at your desk.

How we choose these daily picks

Our product comparisons are built using current retailer data, market analysis and available marketplace feedback to identify the products most worthy of consideration. We do not rely on promotional messaging, manufacturer claims or advertised discounts when making recommendations. Instead, we focus on products that demonstrate strong value, positive seller signals and a credible marketplace track record. Although we have not physically tested every item featured, our methodology is designed to help consumers make informed and confident purchasing decisions. Where performance, safety or durability are especially important, we also encourage checking independent reviews of the exact model.
